close_reason: Replaced 26 mechanical 'always X on the wire' at_type doc-comments with the SHOULD-when-present + §1.3.4 phrasing the bead suggested. Left the bespoke Timestamp doc-comment alone (it already explained the §2.8.1 mechanism specifically). Also rewrote the module-level doc-comment that had the same at_type: String mandatory drift. Pre-commit gate clean (cargo fmt + clippy -D warnings + 58 tests + cargo doc -D warnings). Commit 9eb43f8.
description: Every struct's at_type field carries a doc-comment of the form 'Object type discriminator; always "NameComponent" on the wire.' (e.g. crate-jmap-jscontact-types/src/lib.rs:93, :140, :172, :205, :239, :269, :295, :325, :355, :392, :435, :475, :508, :554, :592, :659, :690, :737, :793, :840, :889, :925, :1004, :1034, :1065, :1094, :1135). The field is typed Option<String> with default + skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none, so the wire form omits @type entirely when the field is None. The 'always' claim is therefore wrong on the wire (None serializes to no @type) and wrong about the type system (the field accepts None). A future contributor reading this either (a) adopts the false belief that the wire always carries @type and writes downstream code assuming so, or (b) submits a PR to change the type to bare String to 'match the doc', breaking the deliberate flexibility for RFC 9553 §1.3.4 defaultType-omission cases (which the AnniversaryDate test at lib.rs:1486 relies on). Fix by replacing each 'always X on the wire' with something like 'Object type discriminator; SHOULD be "X" when present per RFC 9553 §1.3.4 (may be omitted in defaultType positions).'
title: Doc comment 'always "X" on the wire' contradicts at_type: Option<String> across 23 structs
